transcript.user: Tell me a recipe for chocolate cake.

response.text:
Here’s a simple, reliable chocolate cake recipe (one 9-inch round or 8x8-inch square):

Ingredients
- 1 3/4 cups (220 g) all-purpose flour
- 3/4 cup (65 g) unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 cups (400 g) granulated sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk (or any milk)
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water (or very hot coffee for deeper flavor)

Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round pan (or line an 8x8 pan).
2. Whisk dry ingredients: flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
3. Add eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla. Beat until smooth (by hand or with a mixer) about 2 minutes.
4. Stir in boiling water (batter will be thin)—this hydrates cocoa and yields a moist cake.
5. Pour batter into prepared pan and bake 30–35 minutes for a 9-inch pan (35–40 minutes for an 8x8) or until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
6. Cool in pan 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely before frosting.

Simple chocolate frosting
- 1/2 cup (115 g) butter, softened
- 2/3 cup (65 g) unsweetened cocoa powder
- 3 cups (360 g) powdered sugar
- 1/3 cup (80 ml) milk
- 1 tsp vanilla
Beat butter and cocoa, gradually add powdered sugar and milk to reach spreadable consistency, then beat in vanilla.

Notes
- Use hot coffee instead of water for richer chocolate flavor.
- Store covered at room temperature 2–3 days or refrigerate for longer. Enjoy!

Here’s a simple, reliable chocolate cake recipe you can make at home.

Ingredients
- 1¾ cups (220 g) all-purpose flour
- 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar
- ¾ cup (75 g) unsweetened cocoa powder
- 1½ tsp baking powder
- 1½ tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp salt
- 2 large eggs
- 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk (or any milk)
- ½ cup (120 ml) vegetable oil
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 cup (240 ml) boiling water or very hot coffee

Optional chocolate frosting
- ½ cup (115 g) butter, softened
- 2½ cups (300 g) powdered sugar
- ¾ cup (75 g) unsweetened cocoa powder
- 2–3 tbsp milk or cream
- 1 tsp vanilla

Method
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch pan or two 8‑ or 9‑inch round pans.
2. In a large bowl, whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
3. Add eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla; beat until smooth (by hand or with mixer) about 2 minutes.
4. Stir in the boiling water (or hot coffee). Batter will be thin—this is normal.
5. Pour into prepared pan(s). Bake 30–35 minutes for 9x13, or 25–30 minutes for rounds, until a toothpick in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs.
6. Cool in pan 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before frosting.

Frosting (optional)
1. Beat butter until creamy. Add powdered sugar and cocoa gradually.
2. Add milk and vanilla, beating to spreadable consistency. Adjust milk/sugar to desired texture.
3. Spread over cooled cake.

Tips
- Replace boiling water with hot coffee for deeper chocolate flavor.
- Store covered at room temperature 2–3 days or refrigerate for longer; bring to room temp before serving.

transcript.user: What is the difference between cargo worthy and wind and watertight?

response.text:
Short answer:

- Cargo worthy: the container has a valid inspection certifying it fit for transport with cargo. It may show dents, dings or surface rust but meets requirements for carrying freight.

- Wind and watertight: the container keeps weather out (no major holes or leaks) but has not had a cargo‑worthy inspection. It may be a newer one‑trip unit with minor handling marks.

If you need a container for shipping goods, ask for “cargo worthy.” If you only need dry, weather‑protected storage and don’t require a transport inspection, “wind and watertight” may be sufficient.
